origin.description: Text progress bar in the R console.
origin.usage: txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = 1, initial = 0, char = "=", width = NA, title, label, style = 1, file = "")

arguments.name: min, max
arguments.text: Finite extremes. max must be greater than min.

arguments.name: initial
arguments.text: Initial value. NA and out-of-range values are not drawn.

arguments.name: char
arguments.text: The text used to draw the bar. It must have non-zero display width.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Width as a multiple of char. NA uses getOption("width"), and style 3 subtracts 10.

arguments.name: style
arguments.text: 1 appends the bar, 2 redraws it, and 3 adds a percent.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: An open connection, or "" for the console.

origin.details: The manual example sleeps, so the captured call draws style 3 from 0 to 50 percent on a connection.
origin.example:
con <- file(f, open = "wb")
pb <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = 10, style = 3, file = con)
setTxtProgressBar(pb, 5)
close(pb)

translation.description: Write the same text progress bar R writes.
translation.usage: txtProgressBar(min=0, max=1, initial=0, char="=", width=None, title=None, label=None, style=1, file="")

arguments.name: min, max
arguments.text: Finite extremes. max must be greater than min.

arguments.name: style
arguments.text: 1 appends, 2 redraws from the left, 3 draws a percent bar.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: "" writes to stdout. Any open text stream is a connection.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: None uses 80, which is getOption("width") on this R. Style 3 then subtracts 10.

translation.details: close writes the final newline. A value outside the range is ignored.
translation.example:
from utils import close, setTxtProgressBar, txtProgressBar
import io
buf = io.StringIO()
bar = txtProgressBar(min=0, max=10, style=3, file=buf)
setTxtProgressBar(bar, 5)
close(bar)
print(buf.getvalue())
